answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when randomly sampled, independently checked tasks reveal fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and coordinating them to earn rewards without detection risks losing the stake. A lotus-style reputation score may help route work, but should not replace the stake: the tide of cheap new accounts is resisted by costly exposure, while a quill records each verdict for later audits.
